summary: INFY Depth from the web test's packets: a book before any quote shows nothing; the quote then sends the merged view, and a price-only tick sends it again with the cached book.

notes: L1_TICK and L5_TICK of the web test, as Tradejini's binary packets; the refresh is a price-only L1 delta (the web test's ltp=1156.0).

deviations.reason: The web's Tradejini adapter puts its subscription mode number (1, 2, 3) in data.mode; the desktop sends the label (ltp, quote, full). Phase B: follows the web adapter through wire's per-broker switch in the dialect table (Tradejini: the number).

Tradejini sends the trade time in epoch seconds; the web formats it with the server's local time zone into a text such as "2025-11-05 14:25:31" (nxtradstream.py datefmt) and sends that as ltt, where feed timestamps are epoch milliseconds (docs/prompt/websockets-format.md). The desktop sends epoch ms, and leaves ltt out when Tradejini sent no trade time, where the web sends null (Quote, Depth) or "" (LTP).
This L1 (the web test's L1_TICK) carries no circuit limits; the web sends upper_circuit 0 (message.get("ucl", 0)). The desktop leaves it out.
This L1 (the web test's L1_TICK) carries no atp; the web leaves average_price out of Depth, the desktop sends 0.0 (TradejiniFeed::tick unwrap_or). Phase B: mark it absent until Tradejini sends it.
As average_price, for ltq: the desktop sends last_quantity 0.

Tradejini sent one level a side; the web sends that one level (it pads only an empty side to five), the desktop pads each side to five levels with zeros (streaming.rs pad5), a book that was never there.

The web's Tradejini adapter sends OI as oi only; the desktop sends open_interest beside it. Phase B: follows the web adapter through wire's per-broker switch in the dialect table (Tradejini: no open_interest).
